title: Parallel Rollout Approximation for Pixel-Space Autoregressive Image Generation
claim: Our small model beats much larger prior models on a quality-versus-scale trade-off, and produces high-fidelity samples.
layout: 2 panels, left plot and right sample grid, ours in red
description: The figure has two panels. The left panel is a line and marker plot. The x-axis is parameter count (300M, 1B, 2B) and the y-axis is FID, where lower is better. Three baselines are drawn as colored lines with markers: JetFormer (blue circles, 6.64), FractalMAR (orange squares, 6.15) and FARMER (green diamonds, 3.60). They sit high and to the right. PRA (Ours) is drawn in red triangles at the bottom left, with the lowest FID of 1.94, and it is clearly separated from the baselines. Each series has a bold color-matched label and its final value is annotated. The right panel is a 3×4 grid of uncurated ImageNet samples: a cat, ladybug, arctic fox, latte, bee on a flower, golden retriever, stream, border collie, barn, thistle, castle and lighthouse. The eye goes first to the red PRA points in the plot's lower-left corner, then to the photo grid.
caption: Left: FID comparison of pixel-space AR models across parameter scales. PRA achieves substantially lower FID than prior baselines, with PRA-S (135M) already outperforming billionparameter models. Right: Uncurated 256×256 samples generated by PRA-L.
abstract: Pixel-space continuous-token autoregressive (AR) generation directly models images as sequences of raw pixel patches, avoiding discrete tokenization or a separately pretrained tokenizer. However, it faces coupled challenges: high-dimensional patch generation causes large single-step errors, and teacher-forced training creates a train--inference gap that makes these errors accumulate across AR steps. Existing fixes such as $x$-prediction and input noise injection only partially mitigate these issues. Exact rollout training better matches inference-time conditions, but is impractical due to prohibitively slow sequential sampling. We propose Parallel Rollout Approximation (PRA), a scalable framework that addresses both challenges jointly. PRA generates low-dimensional intermediate states and maps them to pixel patches through a one-step denoising pixel decoder, preserving a pixel-in, pixel-out AR interface. The same decoder also constructs inference-like training inputs from perturbed intermediate states through the same intermediate-state-to-pixel path used at inference, while retaining parallel training over positions. On class-conditional ImageNet-1K generation at $256\times256$ resolution, PRA-S with 135M parameters achieves an FID of 2.58, surpassing the previous billion-scale pixel-space AR result of 3.60. Scaling to PRA-L with 511M parameters further improves FID to 1.94, establishing a new SOTA among pixel-space AR models. Beyond generation, PRA achieves higher ImageNet classification probing accuracy than other AR and diffusion baselines, suggesting its potential for unified pixel-space image generation and understanding.
